title: Workshop on Education Economics and Policy (WEEP)
text: WEEP is an annual international workshop bringing together researchers in education economics to discuss new research on education and education policy, exchange ideas and develop research collaborations. The editions from 2026 onwards are supported by the EduGAP research programme.

Exams as Information: Exposure to Math Exams and Later Study Choices
Colin P. Green, Jon Marius Vaag Iversen, Lindsey Macmillan and Gill Wyness (2026).
Working paper.
Using random assignment to mathematics examinations in Norway, we examine how assessment information shapes students’ choices of advanced mathematics, subsequent STEM pathways and higher education outcomes.

title: Research
text:
Research programme
My current research examines school assessment, grading practices, educational choices and their long-run consequences. I am particularly interested in the differences between teacher assessments and external examinations, and how these differences matter for educational opportunities. See EduGAP for the wider research programme.
Additional publications and working papers: NTNU research profile · Google Scholar (publication search).

Economist · Researcher




Research Professor, Centre for Economic Research (SØF), NTNU Social Research
Associate Professor (part-time), Department of Economics, NTNU


I am an applied economist with a PhD in economics from NTNU. My research focuses on the economics of education, with a particular interest in how assessment, school resources and the composition of classrooms affect students’ achievement, educational choices and later labour market outcomes.
My work draws on administrative register data, experiments and applied econometric methods. Alongside my academic research, I lead and contribute to policy-oriented projects on education, labour markets and the financing and organisation of public services. At NTNU, I teach undergraduate statistics and econometrics.


Education economics · Labour economics · Applied microeconometrics · Public economics

My commissioned research combines quantitative analyses, interviews and institutional knowledge to provide evidence for Norwegian public authorities.

title: Research projects
text:
2026–2029 · Principal investigator · Research Council of Norway · NOK 12 million

EduGAP investigates how different forms of assessment affect pupils’ grades, learning, subsequent educational choices and labour market outcomes. The project brings together researchers from Norway, England and the United States.
Grades provide information about achievement but also influence access to educational opportunities. EduGAP studies both functions using longitudinal administrative data, variation in grading practices and differences between examination and teacher-assessment systems. A particular focus is whether assessment practices affect pupils differently according to gender, socioeconomic background and immigrant background.
The research programme focuses on three questions:

How does grading vary across teachers, schools and student groups?
How do teacher assessment and external examinations influence educational pathways and later outcomes?
What can we learn from differences between the Norwegian and English assessment systems?

Research team: Jon Marius Vaag Iversen, Colin Green (NTNU), Lindsey Macmillan and Gill Wyness (UCL), and Richard Murphy (University of Texas at Austin).
I lead the project at the Centre for Economic Research (SØF), NTNU Social Research. The programme combines research collaboration, doctoral training and international dissemination, including WEEP.

text:
Tett på – educational psychological services
The project examines new forms of collaboration between kindergartens, schools and educational psychological services (PPT). My contribution concerns the quantitative evaluation of the reform, including its implications for pupils’ participation and learning outcomes.

Small-group instruction in mathematics
This research investigates the effects of targeted small-group mathematics instruction on early-grade pupils, drawing on a large randomised field experiment in Norwegian schools.

title: Teaching
text:
External examining
I serve as an external examiner across a broad range of economics courses, including microeconomics, macroeconomics and quantitative and applied economics. Institutions I have examined for include the University of Bergen (UiB), the University of Stavanger (UiS), NHH Norwegian School of Economics, BI Norwegian Business School and NTNU.
